public_rationale: The factual components can be investigated: the records document model errors and substantial inference resource demands, alongside useful assistance on a coding task. They cannot settle the full sentence. It supplies neither a defined set of promoted problems nor a standard for what counts as beginning to fix them. Selecting those elements would make the evaluator's choices determine the result.
limitations: This classification concerns the complete assertion, not whether generative AI makes errors or consumes substantial resources.
Selected successes do not disprove failures on many other tasks.
Selected failures would likewise not establish the undefined breadth of the claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI is imperfect and costly to run, yet is held up as a solution to many problems that it can't even begin to fix.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI is imperfect and costly to run, yet is held up as a solution to many problems that it can't even begin to fix.

our_interpretation: Errors and inference resource costs are independently measurable factual components.
The complete assertion does not identify the set of promoted problems, the promoters, or what counts as beginning to fix a problem.
The surrounding examples suggest concerns about coding, image generation and assistants, but do not define the broader set denoted by many problems.
Choosing a task basket and a minimum useful contribution would determine the verdict. There is no sufficiently stable plain reading for grading the complete assertion.
Many problems is a scope qualifier, not a conditional forecast antecedent. The sentence does not assert that generative AI is useless for every task.
criteria.support_condition: No stable whole-claim support test is available without specifying the promoted problems and the standard for useful progress. Errors or high resource costs alone would not establish the concluding assertion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No stable whole-claim contradiction test is available. Demonstrating benefits on some tasks would not disprove failure on many other unspecified tasks.
